verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "It hurts when I pee," which corresponds to dysuria as the main complaint.

Duration: Patient confirms "Uh, six days." Symptoms: "it hurts when I go to the loo, and I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out," consistent with dysuria and foul-smelling urine for 6 days.
Location: "I've got, pain in my tummy" / "In my lower tummy" / "In the middle" (suprapubic). Severity and pattern: Pain rated "Seven" and "Comes and goes," i.e., intermittent 7/10 suprapubic pain.
Hematuria: "I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots." Duration: Doctor asks, "is that just over the last, six days?" and patient answers "Yes."
Eating/drinking: Doctor asks, "have you been able to eat and drink OK?" Patient: "Yes." Fever: "have you had a temperature?..." Patient: "No, not at all" and later reiterates "No fever at all."

Back/loin pain: Doctor asks about back and loin pain and concludes "Um, and no loin pain as well," with no disagreement from patient and earlier denial of back pain. Vaginal discharge: Doctor asks, "any vaginal discharge or, anything like that?" Patient: "No, just the blood spot."
Doctor: "Do you have regular periods?" Patient: "Yes I do."
Doctor asks about triggers: "been doing lots of exercise, been dehydrated, um, been having regular sexual intercourse or anything?" Patient replies "No," denying those triggers.

First episode/UTI history: Doctor: "have you had any problems with your kidneys, or any urine infections?" Patient only mentions IBS and no prior UTIs or kidney issues. Also: "Have you had these symptoms before?" Patient: "No... Never."
Past medical history: Patient states "I had IBS before."

Medication: Patient: "I've had Mebeverine..." Doctor: "Do you take that regularly?" Patient: "Yes." Doctor: "And it, do you take it three times a day?" Patient: "Yes I do." Doctor: "Two hundred milligrams?" Patient: "Yes."
Allergy: Doctor: "Any allergies?" Patient: "Clindamycin." Doctor: "You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK."
Family history: Doctor: "And anyone in your family had any medical problems?" Patient: "No."

Social history: Doctor: "whereabouts, do you live? Do you live with friends, family?" Patient: "I live with friends." Doctor: "And where do you work? What's your job?" Patient: "I'm a support worker."
Alcohol: Doctor: "So how much in a average week?" Patient: "One glass of wine a week." Smoking: Doctor: "And do you smoke?" Patient: "No."
Doctor’s assessment: "it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine" with dysuria and hematuria. This supports an assessment of acute cystitis with hematuria.
IBS stability inferred: Patient uses regular Mebeverine; when asked about bowel habit/weight loss, she replies "No" to changes and weight loss, supporting IBS being stable on Mebeverine.
Doctor: "we can treat this infection... with a course of antibiotics." and "It would just be for three days." Also: "pick them up as soon as you can, and start taking them."
Doctor: "drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day."

Doctor: "you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well, that sometimes helps. And also some, sachets... which just help change the acidity of your urine." These are optional OTC measures.
Doctor: "Have you got a thermometer at home?" Patient: "No." Doctor: "It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature..."

Doctor: "if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling... Then it's very important that we speak to you again." Also: "No, not if you're better. If... they're not resolving with the treatment... Then it's important for us to talk to you in more detail."
Timing: Patient asks how soon prescription will be ready. Doctor: "I would give it longer than that. Give it a, an hour or so."
While the transcript confirms current Mebeverine dosing, there is no explicit advice to "continue" Mebeverine as part of the visit plan; this continuation instruction is not stated.
